partner_context.their_ambition: Crown & Champa operates one of the largest multi-resort groups in the Maldives — Kuredu, Komandoo, Hurawalhi, Kudadoo, Meeru, Veligandu, Vakarufalhi — spanning value-to-premium across several atolls. Its ambition is to run that cluster as a coherent network rather than a set of standalone islands.
partner_context.their_pressure: Operating many islands means operating many transfer arrangements — a patchwork of speedboats and seaplane bookings, each with its own cost, schedule and weather exposure. As the group grows, that fragmentation caps reliability and inflates the cost of the very first impression each resort makes.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A standardised N35 foiling fleet lets Crown & Champa run transfers as one operated network across its resorts — shared vessels, shared training, shared maintenance — turning a fragmented cost centre into a fast, all-weather, branded arrival layer.

hero.title: Navier × Crown & Champa Resorts — arrival as a product, across the operated cluster
hero.subtitle: Re-platforming the airport-to-jetty transfer on foiling-electric vessels — silent, all-weather, zero-emission.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier and Crown & Champa Resorts bring a foiling-electric arrival layer to its Maldivian islands. Navier supplies the software-defined N35 fleet, captain training and the certification path; Crown & Champa Resorts brings the resort relationships and the rollout sequence across its operated cluster. The transfer stops being the weakest link in a premium stay and becomes a branded, all-weather, zero-emission arrival — the same calm quality on every island.

why_now: The Navier × JIH Global program — ~100 vessels, $100M, a three-year phased rollout with the first 5 boats in 2026 — proves, publicly and in Maldivian waters, that foiling-electric works at scale. For Crown & Champa Resorts, that removes the risk: the platform is real and ramping, and the only question is which of its islands to re-platform first.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots between Velana International and the Crown & Champa Resorts jetty — the highest-value leg of the guest journey — with seaplane retained only for the longest outer-atoll legs. The resort books and brands the experience; guests step from jet to foil to villa.

journeys_unlocked.today: 20–45 min in a diesel speedboat, rough in any swell, or a costly seaplane hop.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A smooth, silent ~25-minute foiling transfer direct to the resort jetty — any weather, after dark.

journeys_unlocked.today: Seaplane only — daylight-limited, weather-cancelled, ~$600+ round trip.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: An all-weather, after-dark foiling link to the mid-atolls, complementing seaplane for the longest legs.

journeys_unlocked.today: Congested causeway road or a slow public ferry.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast foiling commuter and visitor link across the capital's lagoon — the resident layer of the same program.

journeys_unlocked.today: A slow tender or a charter booked hours ahead.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: On-demand premium island-hopping between islands, sandbanks and dive sites — the quiet in-stay water layer.

differentiation.why_navier: Crown & Champa's edge is scale — a value-to-premium cluster spread across several atolls, from Kuredu and Komandoo to Hurawalhi and Kudadoo. Navier turns that spread from a liability into a network: one software-defined fleet, one operating standard and one booking layer across every island, replacing a patchwork of separate speedboat and seaplane arrangements.

proof_points.claim: Foiling-electric is already deploying at national scale in the Maldives.
proof_points.evidence: Navier × JIH Global: ~100 vessels / $100M / three-year phasing; first 5 boats in 2026.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

proof_points.claim: Operating many islands today means operating many transfer systems.
proof_points.evidence: A multi-atoll group runs a costly patchwork of speedboats and third-party seaplane bookings, each with its own schedule, weather exposure and standard; a single standardised foiling fleet collapses that into one coherent network.

proof_points.claim: Standardisation is the prize for a large operator.
proof_points.evidence: One vessel platform across the cluster means one captain-training standard, one maintenance model and one guest experience from Meeru to Hurawalhi — the coherence a standalone-island patchwork can't deliver.

objections.concern: We run a lot of islands across atolls — can one platform really cover them all?
objections.response: That's exactly the case for it. The N35 handles the near-Malé and intra-atoll legs, and the Quanta-LR hybrid — up to 700 nm of range — reaches the outer-atoll islands like Hurawalhi and Kudadoo, so the whole cluster runs on one standard instead of a per-island patchwork.

objections.concern: What about charging across so many remote islands?
objections.response: The N35 needs only a berth pedestal at each resort jetty; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging at all — so coverage across the cluster is not gated on building charging at every island.

objections.concern: Won't the outer-atoll resorts still depend on seaplanes?
objections.response: Maldivian seaplanes fly in daylight only, so late guests lose a night. A Quanta-LR foiling vessel reaches the outer atolls and arrives smoothly after dark — turning a forced overnight into a same-night welcome across the group.

phases.label: Phase 1 — flagship-island pilot
phases.narrative: A focused pilot on Crown & Champa Resorts's busiest airport-to-jetty corridor — proving the all-weather N35 arrival on the island where the most guests will feel it.
phases.rationale: Start where transfer volume is highest and the arrival impression matters most.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined N35 foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance and certification path, and an operating playbook already being proven in Maldivian waters.
the_ask.partner_brings: Resort relationships across its operated cluster, the island-by-island rollout sequence, jetty access and the guest-experience standard.
the_ask.next_step: Select Crown & Champa Resorts's first flagship island for a foiling-arrival pilot and define the portfolio rollout sequence.

close.title: The arrival, finally as good as the stay.
close.body: For Crown & Champa Resorts, the transfer has always been the one part of the journey that didn't match the islands. Foiling-electric closes that gap — a silent, all-weather, zero-emission arrival, the same quality on every island.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. Software-defined and autonomy-ready, the same fleet keeps improving over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open ocean and the resort jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. The N35 needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Decarbonization expectations turned diesel transfer fleets into a liability, the platform crossed from prototype to proven service, and a national-scale Maldives program is already live — the resort arrival layer is being re-platformed right now.

end_state.headline: A branded foiling arrival layer across the Crown & Champa Resorts operated cluster.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every Crown & Champa Resorts island in the Maldives, connected to Velana International and to each other by a fast, silent, zero-emission foiling fleet.

steady_state.total_corridors: Airport-to-jetty arrivals + inter-property and in-stay hops
steady_state.platform_mix: N35 for resort arrivals; Pioneer II for short in-stay hops; Quanta-LR for the longest inter-property legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Every guest arrival and in-stay transfer across the portfolio, re-platformed as one branded fleet.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a Crown & Champa Resorts-branded foiling arrival network: jet-to-foil-to-villa on every island, the same calm quality end to end.
